name: Default
author: brodgar
description: This client's own look, key by key and property by property. Installing it changes nothing -- it is the sheet you edit a theme of your own out of.
about: Every site key the client draws at (34 of them), in the order docs/addons/api/ui/style/keys.md lists them, and under each one EVERY property that key honours. A value is what the client itself draws with; null means the client sets none here -- write yours in its place. A null property is absent as far as the client is concerned (JSON null parses to nil, and a nil property is a property the rule does not name), so this file installs as the client's own look exactly, at EVERY interface scale: no value in it is a length or an offset, those being the ones a rule counts in design pixels while the client's own constant is device pixels -- see the README for the five that are null for that reason. Distances would be design pixels and colour components are 0..255. Properties a key IGNORES are left out rather than written null: keys.md's tables say which those are per key. The three layout properties are under treeKeys below, not here -- a site key carrying one is an error.

treeKeys._: Not read by the client -- move an entry into "rules" to use it. A tree key selects WIDGETS rather than a place the client draws, so it carries every drawing property above PLUS the three that lay a widget out, which no site key may have. It also reaches text the game's own resource code draws, which no site key can. A rule covers the widget it names and everything drawn inside it.

shapes._: Not read by the client -- what each property's value looks like, so a null above can be filled in without leaving the file. The prose is on the pages named beside each one.
shapes.font: { builtin: sans|serif|mono|fraktur, size: n, bold: bool, italic: bool, aa: bool } or { asset: "fonts/Inter.ttf", size: n, ... } -- style/text.md#font
shapes.color: { r: n, g: n, b: n, a: n } or [r, g, b, a]. On chat.urgent and chat.speaker instead: { palette: [colour, ...] } or { generate: { step: 0..1, saturation: 0..1, brightness: 0..1 } } -- style/text.md#color
shapes.emboss: false (no relief, which is what lets a colour reach a carved caption) or { texture: <art> } -- style/text.md#emboss
shapes.glow: { color: <colour>, radius: n } -- both required, radius 0 is no halo -- style/text.md#glow
shapes.bg: one <art>, or an array of them in paint order -- style/chrome.md#bg
shapes.border: { <art>, slice: [l, t, r, b] } | { box: "gfx/hud/wnd", mode: tile|stretch } | { color: <colour>, width: n }, each with an optional parts: [ <art with at>, ... ] -- style/chrome.md#border
shapes.padding: n, or [l, t, r, b] -- style/chrome.md#padding
shapes.caption: { at: <corner>, offset: [dx, dy] } -- style/chrome.md#ornaments
shapes.closeButton: an <art> with hover, pressed, at and offset -- style/chrome.md#ornaments
shapes.position: [x, y] or { x: n, y: n } -- tree keys only -- style/geometry.md
shapes.anchor: { to: "screen"|<widget>, at: <corner>, offset: [dx, dy] } -- tree keys only -- style/geometry.md
shapes.size: [w, h] or { w: n, h: n } -- tree keys only -- style/geometry.md
shapes.<art>: { color: <colour> } | { res: "gfx/hud/wnd/lg/bg" } | { asset: "img/panel.png" } | { image: <handle> }, plus at: <corner>, offset: [dx, dy], mode: tile|stretch, and a face per state: hover, pressed, disabled, checked -- style/chrome.md#naming-a-picture
shapes.<corner>: topleft | top | topright | left | center | right | bottomleft | bottom | bottomright
